# opwan_tunnel (Data Source)

The account's tunnel: its client configuration (everything a WireGuard config needs besides the private key) and live status. Fails when the account has no tunnel.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "opwan_tunnel" "this" {}

output "tunnel_up" {
  value = data.opwan_tunnel.this.status.up
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `addresses` (List of String) The tunnel's addresses as /32s, empty until the subscription is active.
- `allowed_ips` (List of String) Suggested `AllowedIPs` of the peer on the client.
- `created_at` (String) When the tunnel was created (RFC 3339).
- `endpoint` (String) The exit's WireGuard endpoint, `host:port`.
- `id` (String) Always `tunnel`.
- `location` (String) The tunnel's location id.
- `mtu` (Number) Suggested client MTU.
- `persistent_keepalive` (Number) Suggested `PersistentKeepalive` in seconds.
- `public_key` (String) The client's WireGuard public key.
- `server_public_key` (String) The exit's WireGuard public key, null until the exit has reported it.
- `state` (String) `pending_payment`, `active`, `suspended` or `canceled`.
- `status` (Attributes) The tunnel's live state, as the exit last reported it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--status))

<a id="nestedatt--status"></a>
### Nested Schema for `status`

Read-Only:

- `last_handshake` (String) The last WireGuard handshake (RFC 3339), null before the first.
- `rate_bps_rx` (Number) Bits per second to you, over the last report.
- `rate_bps_tx` (Number) Bits per second from you, over the last report.
- `throttled` (String) Why the speed is lowered right now: `none`, `burst`, `allowance` or `pacing`.
- `up` (Boolean) A handshake within the last 3 minutes.
- `updated_at` (String) When the exit last reported (RFC 3339), null before the first report.
